articles.title: Harry Kane: Bayern Munich and England striker wins Ballon d'Or after record season
articles.summary: Harry Kane becomes the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.

Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom.

Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three.

"Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn.

"I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now.

"I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination.

"I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better."

England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was "delighted" to see Kane win the award as he hailed the forward's success as a "huge honour".

Prince William, meanwhile, said the former Tottenham Hotspur player was a "brilliant captain" and "remarkable player".

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches.

Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season.

But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals.

Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981.

To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night.

BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies.

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or

In terms of trophies, Kane may have 'only' lifted the German double last season.

But that more than doubled his career trophy total - having also won the Bundesliga the season before.

But in terms of individual output Kane - whose previous best Ballon d'Or finish was 10th - was unmatched last season.

His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five leagues managed.

In fact it was the most anyone has recorded since Cristiano Ronaldo also notched 61 for Real Madrid 11 years ago.

He was the Bundesliga's top scorer with 36 goals - 17 clear of anyone else. In the Champions League he scored 14 for the beaten semi-finalists.

In the German Cup he scored 10 goals, including a hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the final, and he also netted once in the German Super Cup.

No player has ever scored so many goals in a season for Bayern, a club who have had legendary goalscorers like Gerd Muller, Rummenigge and more recently Robert Lewandowski in their ranks.

Kane's 12 goals for England last season - including six at the World Cup - take him up to a total of 73.

Only one player in history from Europe's top leagues has scored more in a season, Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Next on the list are Muller (72 in 1972-73), Cristiano Ronaldo (66 in both 2011-12 and 2014-15), former Brazil striker Ronaldo (66 in 1996-97), Erling Haaland (64 in 2022-23) and Luis Suarez (64 in 2015-16).

Former England striker Alan Shearer recently told BBC Sport: "The winner of the Ballon d'Or should be Harry Kane.

"His numbers for the last 12 to 18 months have been absolutely sensational for Bayern and for England. For that reason, he should get it."

Another ex-Three Lions player Danny Murphy added: "His goalscoring has been relentless, brilliant. He's had one of the best seasons of his career and it'll be a great reward for him if he gets the trophy.

"He's been brilliant at Bayern Munich since he's been there, adapted really well and he's been the best centre forward in the world for the last 12 months."

How rare is winning Ballon d'Or without a top trophy?

The Ballon d'Or was only available to European players from its formation in 1956 until 1995 when it was opened up to everyone.

Since then in four of the seven World Cup years, the Ballon d'Or has been awarded to a world champion - including Messi in 2023 (as the 2022 World Cup was in the winter).

However, that was the first time since 2006 it had happened, with Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Luka Modric all winning since then despite not winning the World Cup that year.

This is only the fifth time in the past 20 years that the Ballon d'Or has not gone to a player who has won either the World Cup, the Champions League or a European Championship/Copa America - with Kane joining Messi (three times) and Ronaldo.

Lamine Yamal, who won the World Cup with Spain, had been one of the favourites but lost out to Kane.

Last year, winning the Champions League helped PSG and France's Ousmane Dembele to the crown.

Kane may have just won the Ballon d'Or but some are already wondering if he is in a good place to retain it next year.

The striker has scored 10 goals in his opening 12 games for Bayern this season.

Throw in six goals in four Nations League games for England and that is a total of 16 in 16 matches so far.

Bayern are unbeaten in the Bundesliga and Champions League this season.

If they were to win a Treble - and Kane keeps scoring at about a goal a game - it would be tough to look past him, especially in a season with no World Cup, European Championship or Copa America.

The last player other than Messi or Ronaldo to win it two years in a row was Marco van Basten in 1988 and 1989.

However, Lamine Yamal will be hoping to make it third time lucky after finishing second twice in two years.

He has started the season in electric form, with 10 goals and 10 assists in 13 games for Barcelona in La Liga and the Champions League.

And Barca are currently favourites to win the Champions League, which could ultimately end up being a deciding factor.

He would be the youngest player to win the Ballon d'Or - aged 20 - if he does lift it next year.

Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe will also fancy his chances of winning for the first time, with 14 goals in 13 appearances for club and country.

The youngest winner remains Brazilian Ronaldo, who was 21 when he won in 1997.

Arsenal, who have never had a Ballon d'Or winner, and Paris St-Germain are two of the other frontrunners to win the Champions League.

articles.body: No hubo fallo. Los 100 de MARCA 2026-27, en su V edición, predijeron con exactitud los ganadores del Balón de Oro 2026 en las tres categorías principales: Balón de Oro masculino, Balón de Oro femenino y mejor entrenador. Las tres categorías a las que más de 200 periodistas de todo el mundo podían votar en el galardón de MARCA. La incertidumbre duró hasta el final... pero finalmente, y pese a las dudas del último día y las variaciones en las apuestas, Harry Kane se coronó en el Balón de Oro 2026 al igual que lo había hecho días atrás en Los 100 de MARCA. El inglés se impuso a Lamine Yamal (segundo) y Mbappé (tercero) en Los 100 de MARCA. En el Balón de Oro, no obstante, cambió el orden del podio: Mbappé fue el segundo y Lamine, el tercero. No hubo debate en el Balón de Oro femenino: Alexia Putellas se llevó su tercer galardón, igualando a Aitana Bonmatí y volviendo a la cima del fútbol mundial. Repitió premio tras haberse coronado también en Los 100 de MARCA hace apenas cuatro días. Luis De la Fuente, seleccionador español y el responsable de dirigir a España a su segunda estrella este pasado verano, se consagró como el mejor técnico tanto en Los 100 de MARCA como en el Balón de Oro, en ambos por delante de Luis Enrique, Flick, Arteta, Kompany o Unai Emery.

articles.title: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas win men’s and women’s Ballon d’Or awards
articles.summary: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas have been named the best men’s and women’s soccer players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.
articles.body: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas have been named the best men’s and women’s soccer players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony. In a glitzy ceremony that was delayed by a rainy and traffic-logged night in London, the Beautiful Game’s great and good gathered to celebrate the very best players in the world. After much debate, it was Kane who was named the men’s Ballon d’Or winner, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the prize. The English striker enjoyed a simply brilliant season last year, scoring 73 goals in 65 competitive matches for club and country – winning the league and cup double with club Bayern Munich. The 33-year-old was emotional during his speech, cheered onto the stage by chants of “Harry, Harry” from a home crowd. “It being here in London as well has made it extra special,” Kane said after winning his first Ballon d’Or. “Thank you very much. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year – some incredible players I was up against.” Kane is the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Meanwhile, Putellas won the women’s award for the third time. The 32-year-old was expected to beat her rivals after another dominant season with Barcelona Femení, where she was the heartbeat of the club’s unrivaled success. She captained the side to a quadruple of trophies – the league title, two domestic cups and the Women’s Champions League – before signing for the London City Lionesses in England this summer. “I don’t know what to say, too many things. Congrats to all the nominees, congrats to all the winners,” Putellas said in her acceptance speech on stage. “That so many Barça players were nominated says a lot about the season we had. … It was my honor to be your captain.” The voting for the men’s and women’s Ballon d’Or is down to selected journalists who vote on behalf of their nation. Each voter ranks their 10 best players, with points distributed on a descending scale depending on their place in the list. Spain and Barça dominate The scene of hundreds of kids damaging security barriers and climbing buildings to get a better view of their heroes arriving on Monday was another reminder of how much this sport means to fans. And many of the biggest names turned up to London’s historic Palladium Theatre, braving the wintry conditions on the red carpet. Yamal drew one of the loudest reactions as he walked up the red carpet, and while he didn’t win the award he most wanted, the 19-year-old was named Young Talent of the Year for a third successive time. It follows a trophy-laden season for both club and country in which the teenager won La Liga for Barcelona and the World Cup for Spain. Meanwhile, Barça’s Vicky López was named the Women’s Young Talent of the Year for a second successive time, capping off a brilliant season with the Blaugrana that dominated across both the men’s and women’s categories. The Spanish and Catalan dominance continued with Spain manager Luis de la Fuente claiming Men’s Coach of the Year after his World Cup glory and Barcelona Femení manager being named Women’s Coach of the Year after guiding his team to practically every trophy. articles.standfirst: Desvelada la posición de los 30 nominados
articles.summary: Desvelada la posición de los 30 nominados
articles.body: El secreto ha sido revelado. Kane se lleva el Balón de Oro 2026 por delante de Mbappé y Lamine. La especulación que ha llenado páginas y páginas durante meses se acabó sobre el escenario del London Palladium para acabar de revelar los últimos nombres de la clasificación de los 30 mejores jugadores de la temporada. Por detrás del inglés se ha clasificado Kylian Mbappé, que ha logrado superar en votos a Lamine Yamal. Por detrás, dos ganadores del Balón de Oro: Rodri y Leo Messi. Esa segunda posición del delantero del Real Madrid es la mejor de su carrera en este galardón. Para el jugador culé, supone bajar un escalón desde el segundo puesto del año pasado. "Para los dos más primeros, Harry Kane y Kylian Mbappé, la diferencia fue mínima este año. La diferencia de puntos entre Kane y Mbappé es menor que la que hubo entre Rodri y Vinicius en 2024. Aquella fue de 41 puntos, y eso no era mucho ni siquiera entonces", reveló Vincent Garcia, redactor jefe de France Football y director de la organización del Balón de Oro. Además, achacó el tercer puesto de Lamine a la división del voto a los jugadores españoles: "Si analizamos los votos, en la selección española que ganó el Mundial, hubo una división entre Rodri y Lamine Yamal. Rodri le quitó algunos votos a Lamine en esta votación en particular. Hubo cierta dispersión de votos entre los españoles. España era un colectivo, por lo que fue difícil destacar una actuación individual. Sabiendo que Lamine Yamal es campeón del mundo pero marcó un solo gol y empezó lesionado, a los miembros del jurado les costó diferenciar a los españoles y destacar a uno sobre otro". La cuenta del Balón de Oro fue descubriendo la clasificación durante la tarde, empezando por el empate en la última posición entre Mané y Saliba y cerrando con Jude Bellingham, posición 11, para desvelar el top 10 durante la gala.

articles.title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years
articles.summary: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or at London ceremony; Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years; England captain hit 73 goals for club and country last season; ex-Tottenham forward beat Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to prize
articles.body:
Michael Owen was the last player from England to receive the prestigious individual accolade in 2001, but Kane's incredible 73-goal haul last season for club and country earned him the award from French magazine France Football.

Bayern Munich forward Kane was a popular winner in the capital and has followed in the footsteps of Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from England.

Kane beat Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to the award.

"Wow, I'm almost speechless," an emotional Kane said on stage. "First of all, thanks again to France Football and the Ballon d'Or for this amazing event. Being in London, it is extra special; it felt like a good omen.

"Thank you to everyone for voting for me. I can imagine it was very tough. Thank you to everyone that voted for me."

Kane, who thanked England, Bayern and former club Tottenham, said: "It's just the journey. For any young boy or girl who wants to achieve their dream, anything is possible.

"I hope my journey, it wasn't straightforward, I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now. I hope that can give you inspiration, and thank you very much."

There was chaos just hours before the ceremony as the Ballon d'Or website published three separate articles naming Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as the winner of the 2026 men's award.

Then, in a further twist, the ceremony was delayed by 45 minutes to an 8.45pm start due to the London traffic.

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher on Kane's Ballon d'Or win:

"Absolutely delighted. What a career he's had, what a player he is, and as a country, we haven't got enough Ballon d'Or winners.

"It's certainly been a long time. My former team-mate Michael Owen was the last to win it in 2001, so it's been a long wait.

"But in terms of Harry Kane, and I think Jude Bellingham, who's going to be a future Ballon d'Or winner, we do have two of the greatest players of their era.

"I'm delighted for Kane and the country."

On the importance of his move from Tottenham to Bayern Munich in winning the Ballon d'Or: "It's a move he needed to make.

"I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one.

"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.

"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."

England boss Tuchel and Prince William send congratulations

England head coach Thomas Tuchel led the tributes to Kane, who became the first Bayern player to win the award in 45 years.

"Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon d'Or!" said Tuchel.

"I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

"To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.

"I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best - scoring goals and winning football matches.'

Prince William, patron of the Football Association, also sent his congratulations.

"What a fantastic achievement and so deserved," the Prince of Wales wrote on Instagram.

"A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments."

Men's 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings in full...

1) Harry Kane - Bayern Munich & England 2) Kylian Mbappe - Real Madrid & France 3) Lamine Yamal - Barcelona - Spain 4) Rodri - Man City/Barcelona & Spain 5) Lionel Messi - Inter Miami & Argentina 6) Khvicha Kvaratskhelia - PSG & Georgia 7) Ousmane Dembele - PSG & France 8) Erling Haaland - Man City & Norway 9) Michael Olise - Bayern Munich & France 10) Fabian Ruiz - PSG & Spain 11) Jude Bellingham - Real Madrid & England 12) Pau Cubarsi - Barcelona & Spain 13) Achraf Hakimi - PSG & Morocco 14) Vitinha - PSG & Portugal 15) Declan Rice - Arsenal & England 16) Ferran Torres - Barcelona/PSG & Spain 17) Vinicius Junior - Real Madrid & Brazil 18) Marc Cucurella - Chelsea/Real Madrid & Spain 19) Joao Neves - PSG & Portugal 20) Willian Pacho - PSG & Ecuador 21) Gabriel - Arsenal & Brazil 22) Lautaro Martinez - Inter Milan & Argentina 23) Nuno Mendes - PSG & Portugal 24) Luis Diaz - Bayern Munich & Colombia 25) Marquinhos - PSG & Brazil 26) Dayot Upamecano - Bayern Munich & France 27) Bruno Fernandes - Man Utd & Portugal 28) Julian Quinones - Al Qadsiah & Mexico =29) William Saliba - Arsenal & France =29) Sadio Mane - Al Nassr & Senegal

Men's Ballon d'Or - Harry Kane (Bayern Munich & England)

Women's Ballon d'Or - Alexia Putellas (London City Lionesses/Barcelona & Spain)

Men's Coach of the Year - Luis de la Fuente (Spain)

Women's Coach of the Year - Pere Romeu (Barcelona)

Men's Young Talent of the Year - Lamine Yamal (Barcelona & Spain)

Women's Young Talent of the Year - Vicky Lopez (Barcelona & Spain)

Men's Striker of the Year - Harry Kane (Bayern Munich & England)

Women's Striker of the Year - Charlyn Corral (CF Pachuca & Mexico)

Men's Goalkeeper of the Year - Unai Simon (Athletic Club & Spain)

Women's Goalkeeper of the Year - Cata Coll (Barcelona & Spain)

Men's Club of the Year - Paris Saint-Germain

Socrates Award (for humanitarian work) - Bukayo Saka (Arsenal & England)

Chaos before Kane was announced as winner

Before Kane's win was announced, the Ballon d'Or website had published three separate articles naming Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as the winner of the 2026 men's award just hours before the ceremony.

The apparent leaks confirmed the top three for the award as chaos descended when a link emerged announcing England captain Kane had received the honour.

"A record-breaking welter of league and cup goals in 2025/26 has propelled Harry Kane to Ballon d'Or success," read the story on the official website of the prestigious France Football prize.

However, further links were subsequently found to articles hailing Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as victors.

All three versions were then taken down before Kane was confirmed to be the winner.

articles.title: Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions
articles.summary: Reflecting on last season's final-day title disappointment, Hearts chairman Calum Paterson calls for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football".
articles.body:
Heart of Midlothian chairman Calum Paterson is calling for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football".

Talking to club media to mark his first year in the post, Paterson spoke with pride about coming so close to a first title in 66 years, but also voiced frustration around how last season's thrilling climax unfolded.

The Edinburgh side topped the Premiership table for 250 days but finished two points behind Celtic after a dramatic final-day defeat in Glasgow.

Lawrence Shankland struck first for the visitors, only for the reigning champions to find two late goals for a 3-1 victory, sparking a pitch invasion from jubilant home fans and a hasty exit for the beaten challengers, who expressed safety fears.

"The final week was difficult on a number of fronts," said Paterson. "Among other things we were disappointed by the unprecedented decision that as the team leading the league at the time of the split had to play our final game away from home.

"The circumstances at the end of that game were, from our perspective, completely unacceptable.

"We took advice and made our concerns very clear to the football authorities. Standing back from it all we'd like to see greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football.

"Standards and processes matter, particularly at important points in the season and there's room for improvement."

The SPFL did explain their scheduling in April, with Celtic due three home matches post-split to Hearts' two. City derbies are ruled out on the final day for public safety reasons, which meant the league body was unable to have both Glasgow or Edinburgh sides play at home on the final two fixture dates.

Having come so close to ending four decades of Old Firm dominance, Paterson added: "The way it ended was really disappointing, especially after everything the players and staff had put into it.

"I think they deserved a better outcome, but we should recognise and pay tribute to them for what they did achieve, which was actually exceptional."

Paterson addressed frustration surrounding the club's communication in the aftermath, stressing that it should have been clearer.

"The supporters should know that we did everything we could to stand up for Hearts and we haven't forgotten what happened last season," he continued.

"Our focus now has to be on putting Hearts in the best position for this season and beyond and communicating better along the way."

Paterson also spoke of the search for increased investment at Tynecastle, where Brighton owner Tony Bloom is a high-profile investor.

"We've had some discussions and those are going well," he said. "I don't want to get ahead of them but if they do conclude successfully, that would be another positive step for Hearts.

"The purpose would be to build a stronger football club fundamentally and to ensure we have resources in place to pursue our ambitions.

"At the same time we're continuing to develop a player trading model which we expect to become an increasingly important contributor to the club's long term financial sustainability."

On the search for a new chief executive to replace Andrew McKinlay who departed in August, Paterson said there are "very strong candidates in the process".

articles.title: Isaac: "Somos una gran familia y lo demostramos cada fin de semana"
articles.standfirst: El lebrijano, con tres dianas, es el máximo goleador del conjunto sevillista
articles.summary: El lebrijano, con tres dianas, es el máximo goleador del conjunto sevillista
articles.body: Isaac Romero, autor del primer gol frente a Osasuna, valoró la victoria del equipo en la zona mixta del Sánchez-Pizjuán. "Sabíamos que teníamos un partido importante, en el que veníamos trabajando mucho esta semana. También hablábamos mucho de dejar la portería a cero. Lo hemos hecho y hemos aprovechado las que hemos tenido", comentó. El MVP del choque reconocía que "salimos un poco regular, yo tampoco me acababa de encontrar en el campo. Después del gol hemos sabido manejar el partido y tener el balón. Somos una gran familia y lo demostramos cada fin de semana en el campo". El lebrijano fue generoso y señaló a su compañero de filas cuando fue cuestionado por su gol: "Me la ha dejado muy bien Fofa y no me lo he pensado, le he pegado como he podido". "Hemos construido una gran familia dentro del vestuario. Nos llevamos todos súper bien, somos chavales jóvenes casi todos. Hablé antes del partido con Peque, que si marcaba me iba al banquillo con ellos a celebrarlo", insistía. Por último tenía palabras para la afición: "Cada partido lo digo, que son el jugador número 12. Están cada semana alentándonos y dándonos todo lo que tienen. Nos dan ese plus de energía". Félix Correia fue el otro goleador del Sevilla frente al conjunto rojillo. "Un partido bellísimo en nuestra casa ante nuestra afición. Es muy importante ganar después del partido ante el Levante y el del Real Madrid. Estamos compitiendo, con buena mentalidad. Era importante ganar y continuar", comentó. "Los primeros quince minutos fueron un poco duros, pero después estuvimos treinta minutos muy bien. En la segunda parte también dominamos el partido. Además, con nuestra gente, es bellísimo estar aquí. Eso es lo más importante". En lo personal, "estoy feliz y con confianza, pero quiero más. Siempre trabajo para más. He hecho un gol, pero ya pienso para en el siguiente partido hacer otro". Félix fue despedido con aplausos por parte de la grada blanquirroja: "Me gusta la gente, la ciudad, las personas del club... Soy muy feliz aquí y el ambiente en nuestra casa es muy bueno. Me gusta jugar aquí".

articles.summary: El canal madridista modificó su programación para emitir un especial de Real Madrid Conecta durante la gala del Balón de Oro
articles.body: Real Madrid TV cambió su programación para seguir en directo los minutos finales de la gala del Balón de Oro. El canal del club blanco dejó a un lado las dos películas que tenía previstas y apostó por un especial de Real Madrid Conecta para acompañar el anuncio de los premiados y, sobre todo, conocer quién se llevaría el galardón masculino. Durante el programa, los tertulianos también pusieron en duda la fiabilidad de las informaciones que habían circulado antes de la gala. "Se han filtrado listas enteras que luego no han sido los que han salido, se han filtrado ganadores que no han sido ganadores, o sea que hay gente jugando al juego del engaño", comentaron, en referencia a las informaciones que habían adelantado supuestos resultados. "Fíjate, qué curioso lo de que la gala por primera vez se celebre en Londres", aseguraron. El debate sobre los méritos deportivos también dejó espacio para las dudas. Al referirse a Rodri, que quedó finalmente cuarto, señaló que había disputado solamente media temporada: "Hay jugadores que están pero no están, o sea, Rodri ha jugado media temporada". En contraposición, destacó el caso de Fabián, al que describió como "el jugador que más títulos ha ganado esta temporada". "Bueno, pues vamos a ver, las esperanzas de los madridistas están puestas, obviamente, en Kylian Mbappé", arrancaron en los minutos de más tensión... y Ronaldo dijo el nombre del ganador. "Bueno, pues los pronósticos sí que han acertado. Sobre todo los pronósticos que se estaban celebrando en Londres. Así que felicidades al jugador del Bayern. Felicidades al jugador de la selección inglesa. Y a la espera de la próxima oportunidad para Kylian Mbappé. No, lo he dicho, felicidades a Harry Kane. Creo que Kylian Mbappé tenía muchas bazas. Pero no es inmerecido ni mucho. Es un gran jugador, una gran trayectoria de Harry Kane, sin duda. Gracias a todos por habernos acompañado este rato. Gracias a vosotros también en este largo Conecta postclásico. Real Madrid ganó en Barcelona y Harry Kane es Balón de Oro. Hasta mañana, chao", zanjaron antes de cortar la emisión y emitir una película (Rescate en Afganistán).

articles.title: England’s Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, Alexia Putellas takes women’s award
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker becomes the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen in 2001.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has completed ‌his long quest for football’s highest individual honour, with the Bayern Munich and England striker winning the Ballon ⁠d’Or after a record-breaking season ⁠that cemented his status as one of the game’s greatest goalscorers.

Kane is the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won it in 2001.

“Wow, wow, wow!” Kane said after taking ⁠the stage on Monday. “I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.

“Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations ⁠to all the winners and nominees tonight, and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve.”

Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or Feminin for the third time.

Kane’s move to Bayern in 2023 brought the team trophies that had long eluded him. In 2025-26, he coupled that success with goalscoring numbers that made him the leading Ballon d’Or candidate.

The England captain produced the most prolific campaign of his life, scoring ‌61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions as the German giants completed a domestic league and cup double.

By the end of the season, Kane had established himself as Europe’s leading goalscorer, turning every competition into a showcase of his finishing ability.

His influence stretched far beyond club football. As England embarked on another attempt to end decades of hurt at the World Cup, Kane once again emerged as the team’s driving force.

He scored six goals during the tournament and led England to the semifinals, combining his clinical finishing with the leadership and composure that have defined his international career.

In many ways, the award represents the culmination ⁠of a remarkable journey. Few players have experienced a career arc quite like Kane’s.

Once struggling to ⁠establish himself at Tottenham Hotspur as a youngster, being sent out on numerous loans, he developed into one of the most complete centre forwards of his generation, capable of scoring every type of goal while also functioning as a playmaker.

The Ballon d’Or has often rewarded players whose success was built on flair and spectacle, ⁠but Kane’s triumph is a tribute to consistency, intelligence and productivity on an exceptional scale.

His ⁠numbers were almost impossible to ignore.

Kane finished the campaign with 73 goals for club ⁠and country, a total rarely seen in the modern era. More importantly, those goals arrived in moments of genuine significance, helping Bayern collect trophies and driving England deep into the biggest tournament in the sport.

The competition for this year’s award was fierce. Kylian Mbappe broke World Cup scoring records. Lamine Yamal helped Spain to World Cup ‌glory. Yet voters ultimately chose Kane, whose excellence lasted the entire season.

At 33, Kane has finally claimed the game’s highest individual honour, adding a Ballon d’Or to a legacy that already places him among football’s greatest strikers as England’s all-time leading marksman and their record ‌World ‌Cup scorer.

Putellas was presented with the women’s award after winning the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign, in addition to the Spanish Super Cup. She moved to Women’s Super League side London City Lionesses in July, after 14 years at Barca.

articles.title: Harry Kane wins first Ballon d'Or, Alexia Putellas takes 2026 Ballon d'Or Féminin in delayed ceremony
articles.summary: Kane won the honor for the first time after a massive season with Bayern Munich; Putellas took the award for the third time in her career in an overlong, Spa...
articles.body:
Harry Kane has won the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or, capping off a career year for the 33-year-old England and Bayern Munich striker. Spanish striker Alexia Putellas took the Ballon d'Or Féminin, her third time winning the honor, in what became a very Spain-heavy night at the London Palladium on Monday.

In a monster season with the dominant German club, Kane scored 61 goals across all competitions for Bayern, including 36 goals in 31 Bundesliga games. Meanwhile, as captain for the Three Lions, Kane led England to its best World Cup result in six decades, with the team earning third place.

Kane was emotional as he earned the award, the first of his career.

"I'm almost speechless," Kane said before thanking his teammates in the audience and his family, among others, and calling Bayern Munich "an honor to play for."

Kane beat out two soccer heavyweights, French captain Kylian Mbappé and young Spanish phenom Lamine Yamal, for the award. Though Yamal again fell short of the top award — he finished second to Ousmane Dembélé last year, and third this year — he did earn his third straight Kopa Trophy, given to the best player under 21.

Kane was also awarded the Striker of the Year award alongside Mexico and CF Pachuca striker Charlyn Corral, given to the top scorers internationally.

On the women's side, Putellas emerged victorious for the Ballon d'Or Féminin after a even more competitive race. Putellas, an attacking midfielder for London City Lionesses (formerly Barcelona) and the Spanish national team, returned to the podium three years after winning the award twice in 2021 and 2022. That gap was caused in part by an ACL tear that sidelined her for the better part of two years.

In her speech, Putellas noted the number of Barcelona players that were nominated for the award — five of the 10 finalists play for Barça — and thanked her family and friend for helping her back from her injury.

"I had a tough time and had to learn to walk again on my knee and you were all there for me, helping me to enjoy the sport again and make me the player I am today," Putellas said.

Three-time winner Aitana Bonmatí, Putellas' teammate from Barcelona and the Spanish team, missed significant time last year with a broken leg; as a result, she was left off the shortlist.

That seemed to leave things open for a first-time winner, with players like Manchester City's Khadija "Bunny" Shaw (of Jamaica) and Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor (of Poland) among the other nominees. But Putellas' importance to a dominant Barcelona squad last season was enough to keep the trophy in Spanish hands.

Though Kane and Putellas ended up taking the final awards, it took quite a while to get to that point. The ceremony itself, which was delayed by 45 minutes, dragged significantly and began to lose control of its audience as time went on. One switch to commercial, before the women's Ballon d'Or was named, was met with audible boos from an audience that had been surprisingly patient throughout the delays.

The lengthy ceremony came after another snafu, when the official Ballon d'Or website posted stories about Kane, Yamal and Mbappé — the three top finalists — winning the award hours before the final result was announced. The stories, which appeared to be drafts in case of the different winning results, were deleted before the ceremony.

Overall, it was a Spain-heavy night, with eight of the 12 award winners involved with La Liga clubs, La Liga F clubs or the Spanish national teams. Alongside Putellas, FC Barcelona was named the best women's club, with goalkeeper Cata Coll, head coach Pere Romeu and young star Vicky López taking their respective awards.

The men's Spanish national team, after winning its second World Cup title this summer, was also well-represented: In addition to Yamal, coach Luis de la Fuente and goalkeeper Unai Simón also took home honors.

U.S. women's national team and Gotham FC midfielder Rose Lavelle, the only American on the shortlist for either award, finished in 27th place out of 30 total nominees. (The Ballon d'Or, which is awarded by "France Football" magazine and voted on by a number of international journalists, often tilts in favor of European players, making the lack of Americans pretty familiar.)

Another USWNT starter, 19-year-old OL Lyonnes midfielder Lily Yohannes, was one of five finalists for the young talent award. Yohannes lost out to Barcelona's Vicky López, who earned the Kopa Trophy for the second straight year.

Two star NWSL forwards on the list, Kansas City Current's Temwa Chawinga and Orlando Pride's Barbra Banda, finished 10th and 18th, respectively.

Inter Miami and Argentina star Lionel Messi, in what might be his final Ballon d'Or nomination after the legendary midfielder announced his international retirement , finished in fifth place in the men's voting. Messi has won the award a record eight times across his career, with his first win in 2009.

Another interesting nominee was World Cup fan-favorite Vozinha, the 40-year-old goalie for the Cape Verde national team who became a breakout star during the tournament and became one of the nominees for Goalkeeper of the Year. He ended up losing out to Spain's Unai Simón.

Young talent: Vicky López (Barcelona, Spain), Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain)

Coach of the Year: Pere Romeu (Barcelona Femení), Luis de la Fuente (Spain men's national team)

Goalkeeper of the Year: Cata Coll (Barcelona, Spain), Unai Simón (Athletic Bilbao, Spain)

Club of the Year: FC Barcelona (women's), Paris Saint-Germain (men's)

Top scorer: Charlyn Corral (CF Pachuca, Mexico), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich, England)

Ballon d'Or Féminin: Alexia Putellas (London City Lionesses, Spain)

Ballon d'Or: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich, England)

articles.summary: El entrenador del Sevilla consideró que incluso se quedaron "cortos en la portería contraria"
articles.body: Luis García Plaza compareció tras la quinta victoria del Sevilla esta temporada, la tercera en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, donde logró imponerse a Osasuna (2-0). "Nos ha costado al principio. El otro día contra el Racing eran mucho más directos y creíamos que con los dos puntas en la presión nos valía para coger esa segunda jugada. Sin embargo, han sido más combinativos y nos ha costado leerlo. En cuanto lo hemos ajustado, el equipo ha estado muy bien", explicó el técnico blanquirrojo. Desarrollo del partido: "La primera parte es muy buena. Después de esos 20 minutos hemos estado jugando en campo contrario, siempre muy adelantados. Y después otra vez, al principio del segundo tiempo, es normal que ellos aprieten un poquito, pero hemos tenido el control del partido. Creo que nos hemos quedado cortos en la portería contraria y es una victoria merecida". 17 puntos: "La medida de puntos es altísima, son 1,7 por partido. Solo hemos perdido con los tres gigantes y con los demás competimos muy bien. Los chicos se esfuerzan al máximo, lo dan todo. Hemos marcado en todos los partidos. Somos capaces de generar varios registros, tanto de transición, de balón parado e incluso creo que estamos creciendo mucho en el juego organizado, siempre partiendo de jugar en campo contrario, sobre todo en casa. Pero esto es muy largo". Portería a 0: "A mí el único partido en que me ha sorprendido recibir tres goles es el del Levante, con todo el respeto. Hemos estado muy bien defensivamente en todos los partidos quitando los tres grandes, que es algo hasta normal, sobre todo por nuestra manera de jugar porque creo que es una tontería cambiar. El equipo está muy comprometido. El trabajo de Lucas y de Isaac ha sido impresionante, incluso el de Ejuke. Compromiso y a partir de ahí, crecer". Posición de Isaac: "Creo que encaja muy bien en ese perfil. Y después, tengo una apuesta personal con él de goles. Espero que la cumpla. Pero a mí de segundo delantero me gusta. Muchas veces he tenido que jugar solo porque al principio no teníamos delanteros. No quiere decir que vaya a jugar siempre porque también nos cabe jugar en medio con cualquiera. Kocho y Guri ya entrenan mejor, y Manu está a un nivel muy bueno y otra vez ha salido y ha estado genial".

articles.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player
articles.summary: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or to become first Englishman to land award in 25 years; Bayern Munich and England captain's Ballon d'Or victory called 'Cinderella story' by Tim Sherwood; watch Bayern vs Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
"This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports .

"He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking, 'Are we talking about the same kid?'

"There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further.

"I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest."

The Bayern Munich striker has become the first English Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years and just the fifth in its history.

The last English winner, Michael Owen, had a simpler route to the top, winning it aged 22 in 2001, just four years after his senior debut at Liverpool.

Kane's win has come at the age of 33, some 15 years after his senior debut on loan at Leyton Orient in League One.

"I think we have to highlight his journey," says Sherwood, who Kane thanked on stage when collecting the Ballon d'Or.

"Even when we go back to Michael (Owen), he was a superstar as a kid, and he got the opportunities at a very young age at Liverpool, which is a giant football club.

"Kane came through the hard way, really. He was a player who wasn't universally loved.

"He's not like a Max Dowman, for instance, who is a superstar at 16 years of age.

"He (Kane) struggled to get some game time and to get a manager to really, really buy into what he had."

Kane even mentioned his tough path to the top in his Ballon d'Or acceptance speech.

He said: "My journey wasn't straightforward; I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now."

For Sherwood, it was those low-key loan spells at Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester that have turned Kane into the world's top player.

"I hear a lot of people talking about failed loans," he says, "but we never felt like that because we felt that him playing in U21 football was a waste of time.

"They were really good loans, and those loans were the reason why we've got a player like that."

Kane was out in the cold at Spurs until Andre Villas-Boas' sacking, when Sherwood's subsequent arrival opened the door.

He handed Kane his first-ever Premier League start - and the then-20-year-old took his chance as he scored the opener in a 5-1 home win over Sunderland in April 2014.

"He wasn't getting anywhere unfortunately," Sherwood says. "He wasn't around the first-team squad, so I suppose it's a sliding doors moment that I managed to take over until the end of the season and I managed to give him a stage where he could perform."

Kane has hit nearly 550 goals for club and country to become Tottenham's record scorer, England's all-time scorer, England's leading World Cup scorer and the top English scorer in Champions League history.

His incredible goalscoring feats hit new heights last season as he plundered 73 goals in all competitions.

Sixty-one of those came for Bayern in all competitions, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues last season. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

For Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher, Kane's £100m move from Spurs to Bayern in the summer of 2023 has allowed him global recognition and respect.

"It's a move he needed to make," Carragher tells Sky Sports .

"I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one.

"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.

"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."

The Bayern move has delivered the trophies Kane so desperately craved.

Despite winning three Premier League Golden Boots at Spurs and becoming their all-time top scorer, personal honours were never the aim of the game for Kane, according to Sherwood.

His trophyless career at N17 is what drove Kane to join Bayern, where he has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a German Cup.

"The boy loves Tottenham," Sherwood says. "He wanted to win there, but he was winning individual accolades at Spurs, and it wasn't enough for him.

"When we all grow up, we all want to be footballers, and we don't want to be footballers because we want to be rich. There are possibly some players like that now, but that certainly wasn't his motivation.

"He wanted to go to a team that could win, and he picked Bayern, and we have to say it's been a good choice."

Sherwood adds: "He's a 100 per cent team man. If I told you he would rather win the Champions League and the Bundesliga title than the Ballon d'Or for himself, that would be the truth.

"Not every player would say that, but I genuinely believe that that is the measure of the man and that's what you're talking about, and that's why he's such a dream to manage.

"The work rate and the example he shows to any young kids coming through, and to genuinely go around the houses to try and make it, and he certainly made it."

Kane continues to break record after record in Germany.

He is the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, has the most goals in his first 100 Bundesliga appearances and is the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goal contributions.

It is that last stat where Kane has proven he is more than just a goal scorer. His excellent vision, awareness and superb passing range make him an exquisite playmaker.

This was on show recently in Bayern's 2-2 Champions League home draw against Arsenal as Kane, who spent much of the game dropping deep, sumptuously set up Alphonso Davies for an equaliser with a pinpoint ball from inside the centre circle.

His assist ability has been on display for years, where at Spurs he claimed the Premier League Playmaker of the Season award in the 2020/21 campaign.

So, does his all-round game combined with his records and this Ballon d'Or prize make him England's greatest-ever player? Not for Carragher, who puts a fellow English Ballon d'Or winner ahead of him.

"I would still always put Bobby Charlton as the greatest England player ever," he says.

"He's won the World Cup. He's won the Champions League with Manchester United. As a midfield player, he was the leading goalscorer for a very long time for both United and England.

"I'd still always say Bobby Charlton, because right now this England team, even though it's been a golden period for us, Harry Kane and the others still haven't got their hands on a trophy, and that's what Bobby Charlton did."

Kane, who needs just one cap to become England's most-capped player, and although there are plenty of trophies to be won, Sherwood believes there is a longer-term goal in Kane's thinking.

"I believe he will come back for that individual accolade to be the Premier League top scorer in the future, maybe in a couple of years' time," the ex-Premier League-winning captain says.

Kane is 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's all-time Premier League record of 260 goals.

"He will only come back to a team he believes can win," says Sherwood. "At the moment you're looking at Man City with the troubles they've got, so Liverpool possibly, that could be a chance for him.

"Tottenham could be in the frame if they start progressing. Manchester United could be in the frame, but they've got a long way to go to prove that they can win anything as well.

"I'm not sure it's ever going to be Chelsea or Arsenal because of the Tottenham connection.

"So, it's on a positive note for Tottenham fans if they can start progressing and you can prove to him that he can come back and he can possibly have a good chance of winning at your club as he will have at Liverpool, Man Utd and Man City - but we don't know what's going to happen with them - then there's an opportunity he might come back and see out his career where he started it."

It seems a fitting final chapter in Kane's Cinderella story.

articles.title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or, ends England’s 25-year wait and makes history as first player to win two individual awards in one night
articles.summary: Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or and Gerd Müller Trophy, ending England's 25-year wait for a Ballon d'Or winner. Achieving a record-breaking 73 goals, Kane is the first player to win two individual awards in one night at the prestigious gala.
articles.body: Harry Kane has spent years chasing the biggest prizes in football, and his latest achievement has taken him somewhere no player has reached before. The Bayern Munich striker has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner, while also claiming the Gerd Müller Trophy at the same ceremony. His 73 goals for club and country made the case, with the resulting double giving an extraordinary season an equally historic finish.Kane ends England’s 25-year Ballon d’Or waitThe Leytonstone-born forward becomes the fifth Englishman to win the men’s Ballon d’Or, following Sir Stanley Matthews in 1956, Sir Bobby Charlton in 1966, Kevin Keegan in 1978 and 1979, and Michael Owen in 2001. Kane’s seventh Ballon d’Or nomination proved to be the charm, with the Bayern Munich striker finally claiming the coveted prize after years of falling short amid a lack of major team trophies. His victory ends England’s 25-year wait for a winner and makes him the first player to collect the award as a Bayern Munich player.Matthews was the inaugural winner when the prize was introduced in 1956, while Keegan remains the only Englishman to win it twice and the only one to claim it in consecutive years. Keegan also previously held the distinction of being the only English winner playing for a foreign club, having collected both awards while representing Hamburg in Germany.Kane’s 2026 triumph follows a season in which he scored 73 goals across 65 competitive appearances for Bayern and England, alongside eight assists. He finished with the second-highest single-season goal tally by a player in the 21st century, averaging more than a goal per appearance across the campaign.The final men’s Ballon d’Or rankings placed Kylian Mbappé second and Lamine Yamal third, while Lionel Messi ended the night in fifth.The final top 10:Harry KaneKylian MbappéLamine YamalRodriLionel MessiKhvicha KvaratskheliaOusmane DembéléErling HaalandMichael OliseFabián RuizKane was joined in the winners’ spotlight by his female counterpart, Alexia Putellas, who won the 2026 Ballon d’Or Féminin. The Barcelona legend claimed the women’s prize for a record-equalling third time, following her victories in 2021 and 2022, keeping the award in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year.Putellas was rewarded for a spectacular 2025–26 campaign with Barcelona Femení, captaining the club to a historic quadruple that included the UEFA Women’s Champions League, before moving to London City Lionesses.Bayern’s 61 goals explain the scale of his seasonKane’s club campaign supplied the largest share of his remarkable total, with 61 goals and seven assists across 51 appearances for Bayern in all competitions. His Bundesliga record was particularly striking: he scored 36 times in 31 appearances, including 26 starts, at a rate of one goal every 66.1 minutes.He carried that finishing into Europe, scoring 14 goals in 13 Champions League appearances as Bayern reached the semi-finals, while also contributing two assists in the competition. His domestic cup campaign proved even more prolific, with 10 goals in six DFB-Pokal appearances as Bayern secured their 21st triumph in the competition, including a hat-trick from Kane in the final against Stuttgart.He also scored once in one appearance in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup, completing a season in which his goals came across every major competition Bayern contested. His combined rate of one goal or assist every 59 minutes reflected how frequently he influenced matches, whether by finishing moves himself or creating opportunities for teammates.The season also brought Kane a second European Golden Shoe and the Bundesliga’s Torjägerkanone for the third consecutive campaign, reinforcing his position as the division’s leading scorer. His individual recognition now extends beyond those domestic honours, with the Ballon d’Or placing him at the top of world football’s annual individual rankings.The Gerd Müller Trophy makes it a historic doubleKane’s second award on the night was the Gerd Müller Trophy, which recognises the leading goalscorer across club and international football during a European season. Introduced in 2021 as the Striker of the Year award, it was renamed in 2022 to honour the legendary German forward, who died in 2021.Kane had already won the trophy in 2024 and collected it again in 2026, but adding the main Ballon d’Or created a first in the ceremony’s history. No player had previously won two individual awards during the same Ballon d’Or gala, although organisers had confirmed that the rules permitted multiple honours because each award is decided through a separate voting process.The possibility had been there, but Kane’s 73-goal campaign turned it into reality, making him the first player to claim both prizes at one ceremony. His achievement also gives the Gerd Müller Trophy a different significance, moving beyond recognition for goals alone to accompany the sport’s most prestigious individual award.England’s record scorer is closing in on another landmarkKane’s contribution to England’s season further strengthened his case, with 12 international goals taking his career tally for the national team to 91. He became England’s record goalscorer in 2024, and his latest run has brought the century mark within reach.Six of those goals came at the 2026 World Cup, where three were match-winners and Kane overtook Gary Lineker to become England’s leading scorer in World Cup finals. Lineker himself had been nominated for the Ballon d’Or five times, adding another historical connection to Kane’s latest achievement.During the period used to assess the Striker of the Year award, Kane scored for England every 97.7 minutes. Since September 2025, he has also accounted for 32.4 per cent of England’s goals in matches he played, underlining how central he remains to the national side’s attack.At 33, Kane has now collected the Ballon d’Or, the Gerd Müller Trophy, another European Golden Shoe and a third consecutive Bundesliga scoring title in a season that has reshaped his place in football history. England’s wait for another winner is over, and no player has ever left a Ballon d’Or ceremony with the same two individual honours that Kane has claimed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Arrasate: "El Sevilla ahora mismo es mejor que nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El técnico rojillo reconoció la superioridad del rival
articles.summary: El técnico rojillo reconoció la superioridad del rival
articles.body: El técnico de Osasuna, Jagoba Arrasate, lamentó la derrota por 2-0 en el campo del Sevilla, un rival del que destacó que "defiende muy bien hacia delante", una faceta del juego en la que admitió que les superó por completo, aparte de que su equipo fue "muy previsible" en ataque. "La derrota es justa, el Sevilla es justo vencedor", reconoció tras el encuentro Arrasate, quien explicó que Osasuna comenzó bien, pero "a partir de los veinte minutos" perdió "fluidez", y añadió que "con el gol de ellos" tuvieron que "asumir más espacios en la segunda parte y ha llegado el 2-0" del conjunto andaluz en la recta final. El técnico vizcaíno dijo que esperaban que el Sevilla saliera "con dos puntas", como ha hecho otras veces "en casa", y "la duda era si sería Ure o Stassin" porque "con el medio campo que tiene se puede permitir jugar" con ese sistema y, al final, les "ha salido bien con el gol de Isaac Romero". "Cuando hemos circulado el balón rápido, hemos tenido oportunidades y más opciones, pero ellos son un equipo muy intenso, defienden hacia delante, y hay que aceptar la realidad. El Sevilla ahora mismo es mejor que nosotros, sobre todo en defender de esa manera, así que aprendizaje de la derrota y a seguir", recalcó Jagoba Arrasate.

articles.title: El Barça femenino, España y Harry Kane
articles.standfirst: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Vicky López, Lamine Yamal, Pere Romeu, Luis de la Fuente, Cata Coll, Unai Simón… La gala del Balón de Oro avanzaba y España iba al copo a través de su selección campeona del mundo y del Barça femenino, ese prodigio de equipo al que aún le quedaban por recoger dos premios: el de mejor club del año (¿y cómo no?) que recogió un feliz Laporta tras el paso por el escenario de Bukayo Saka, ganador del ‘Sócrates’. Y aún quedaba, como el galardón mayor femenino, el Balón de Oro para Alexia Putellas, tercero que obtiene. Al Barça femenino sólo se le escapó el premio, de pura contabilización, a la máxima goleadora, que se llevó la mexicana Charlyn Corral, del Pachuca, por sus 49 goles en 49 partidos, que también regó de tantos nuestro fútbol en su paso por el Levante y el Atlético de Madrid. El ya largo en el tiempo mimo del Barça a esta sección del club fue brillante y merecidamente ensalzado en este acto universal. Esa apuesta le da al Barça felicidad e imagen de vanguardia en la inclusión. Fue magnífico el parlamento de Unai Simón al recoger el premio al mejor portero, con el mérito de haberlo logrado desde el Athletic, de gran tradición de porteros sensacionales (Blasco, Carmelo, Iribar, Zubizarreta…) pero sin la presencia internacional de otros clubes. En cuanto a Luis de la Fuente, no cabía la menor duda. Ha hecho un equipo magistral, campeón de la Copa del Mundo con un juego pulcro que enalteció este deporte, sobre todo en la final, cuando sobrevivió a las brusquedades de Argentina. Y finalmente, ya cerca de la medianoche (la gala empezó con un retraso inconcebible en un acto comprometido con tantas televisiones del mundo), se desveló el premio mayor, el de mejor jugador masculino, que fue para Harry Kane. Buena elección y muy apropiada para el fasto y el escenario, puesto que estábamos en Londres y se conmemoraba el primero, en el ya lejano 1956, el genial Stanley Matthews. Habrá malicias por ello, pero lo encuentro perfectamente justo. Un delantero grande, con panorama y buen pase cuando se echa atrás y formidable cuota de goles: 73 en el último curso.

articles.title: Ciudadano Kane
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Kane no ganaba títulos porque jugaba en el Tottenham. Llegó al Bayern y empezó a ganarlos. Así de sencillo, por muchas bromas y veras que hicieran a su costa los entendidos de sofá o teclado. Porque, por mucha importancia que se quiera dar a lo individual, y precisamente el Balón de Oro lleva al paroxismo esa tendencia, el fútbol sigue siendo un deporte colectivo. Y sí, es cierto que el equipo inglés conquistó la Europa League justo la temporada 24-25, primera sin Harry, pero fue después de 17 años de sequía y coincidiendo con la primera Bundesliga del punta con el Bayern, que recuperaba así una hegemonía extraviada precisamente la campaña anterior. Kane firmó una temporada 25-26 espectacular para justificar el premio que recibía anoche en Londres. No se trata sólo de las 73 dianas, que también, evidentemente, sino de que con ellas repitió suerte en el campeonato doméstico, de que hasta tres correspondieron a la final de Copa (las únicas que se certificaron en aquel duelo con el Stuttgart), de que marcó en todas las eliminatorias Champions incluida esa semifinal agónica ante el PSG o de que fue decisivo para que Inglaterra se plantara entre las cuatro mejores del Mundial (con la terrible sensación de que hubiera sido finalista de no mediar una pájara increíble de su seleccionador). Kane seguiría siendo un jugador espléndido en un hipotético fútbol sin goles, véase la asistencia a Davies hace menos de una semana con la que acuchilló a un Arsenal que presume con razón de tener la mejor defensa de Europa. Preciosa... y precisa. Harry ha ido creciendo con los años, toda esta broma le pilla con 33, hasta convertirse por su capacidad de asociación y/o por su capacidad de trabajo en una referencia para todo el campo, no sólo para el área. Kane no es polémico, además, cuestión que por lo visto también cuenta para el galardón. Y, aspecto que se agradece muchísimo visto lo visto, no ha dado la turra para ganarlo. Se ponga como se ponga ahora el que se ponga, lo de Lamine o Mbappé no había por dónde cogerlo, esa sobredosis de ego para reclamar qué había de lo suyo mientras los tipos que se ponen la misma camiseta contemplaban atónitos los acontecimientos. Efectivamente, como escribía un compañero en estas mismas páginas, no se conoce afición que haya acudido a la fuente de turno para festejar un reconocimiento que no tenga forma de título. Kane, en ese sentido, lo tenía claro cuando hace poco más de un mes MARCA le preguntó por sus opciones de ganar el Balón: "No me gusta demasiado hablar de mí mismo [...] No está en mis manos. Depende de las personas que votan". Ni campaña, ni autopromoción. Ha sido justo después de conquistarlo cuando por fin se ha permitido un desahogo que dice mucho también sobre el tipo: "Trabaja duro en silencio. Deja que el éxito sea tu ruido". Seguramente había argumentos futbolísticos para defender diferentes resoluciones, la de Yamal, la de Kylian, algunas otras, pero entre tanto griterío se aplaude que un tipo ame la discreción. Ciudadano Kane, futbolista ejemplar.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Full winners list, men’s and women’s rankings led by Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas
articles.summary: The Ballon d'Or 2026 ceremony in London celebrated footballing excellence, featuring Harry Kane's first win and Alexia Putellas' third, alongside record milestones and the dominance of Spanish football.
articles.body: The 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or ceremony brought the peak of footballing excellence to London’s historic Palladium Theatre. Held in honour of Sir Stanley Matthews:the legendary inaugural winner of the trophy in 1956:the gala marked the very first time the prestigious awards were presented on English soil. The evening ultimately belonged to Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas, who claimed the ultimate individual crowns amidst a night of record-breaking milestones, dominant displays from Spanish football, and historical sweeps.Harry Kane bridges a quarter-century gap for English FootballHarry Kane claimed his maiden Men's Ballon d'Or, edging out Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona prodigy Lamine Yamal following a spectacular season for both club and country.Kane's triumph makes him the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Men’s Ballon d'Or, succeeding Michael Owen who last lifted the trophy in 2001. By winning football's ultimate individual prize, Kane joins an elite pantheon of English icons that includes Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, and Kevin Keegan. Further down the list, Lionel Messi finished fifth in what is widely considered his final career nomination following his international retirement announcement.Men’s Ballon d’Or: Top 10 rankingsHarry Kane: Bayern Munich / EnglandKylian Mbappé : Real Madrid / FranceLamine Yamal : Barcelona / SpainRodri : Barcelona / SpainLionel Messi : Inter Miami / ArgentinaKhvicha Kvaratskhelia : Paris Saint-Germain / GeorgiaOusmane Dembélé : Paris Saint-Germain / FranceErling Haaland : Manchester City / NorwayMichael Olise : Bayern Munich / FranceFabián Ruiz : Paris Saint-Germain / SpainAlexia Putellas reclaims her throne with record-equalling third titleIn the women's category, Alexia Putellas officially reclaimed the global crown, returning to the absolute apex of the women's game ahead of her Barcelona teammate Ewa Pajor and Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw.With this victory, Putellas captures a record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Féminin (adding to her wins in 2021 and 2022), tying her Spain teammate Aitana Bonmatí for the most titles in the history of the women's award. Crucially, while she spent the core voting period dominating with FC Barcelona, her summer move makes her the first-ever winner technically affiliated with a Women’s Super League (WSL) side, representing the London City Lionesses.Women’s Ballon d’Or: Top 10 rankingsAlexia Putellas: London City Lionesses / SpainEwa Pajor: Barcelona / PolandKhadija Shaw: Manchester City / JamaicaMelchie Dumornay: OL Lyonnes / HaitiPatri Guijarro: Barcelona / SpainCaroline Graham Hansen: Barcelona / NorwayPernille Harder: Bayern Munich / DenmarkClàudia Pina: Barcelona / SpainAlessia Russo: Arsenal / EnglandTemwa Chawinga: Kansas City Current / MalawiBarcelona's La Masia Academy solidifies youth strangleholdThe youth categories showcased the unmatched talent production pipeline of Barcelona's La Masia, with the club securing both the men's and women's U21 honours.Lamine Yamal (Men’s Young Player of the Year): Yamal made unprecedented footballing history by retaining the Kopa Trophy to win it for a third consecutive time (2024, 2025, and 2026). Since the award's inception by France Football in 2018, no other player has ever won it more than once.Vicky López (Women’s Young Player of the Year): Continuing the club's complete dominance on the youth circuit, López retained the crown to secure her second consecutive young women's player of the year award.Major category winners and historic milestonesThe secondary awards highlighted historic tactical triumphs, unmatched club dominance, and remarkable humanitarian efforts across the globe.Men’s Striker of the Year (Gerd Müller Trophy) – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich / England): Kane completed a double-trophy evening by securing the top striker accolade. This marks the second time Kane has won the Gerd Müller Trophy, having previously shared the honour back in 2024.Women’s Striker of the Year (Gerd Müller Trophy) – Charlyn Corral (CF Pachuca / Mexico): A historic victory for Liga MX Femenil, Corral became the first player playing outside of Europe's top divisions to claim this global goalscoring metric.Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year (Yashin Trophy) – Unai Simón (Athletic Club / Spain): Simón was awarded the top goalkeeper prize primarily for his spectacular penalty heroics and stellar defensive leadership guiding Spain to their 2026 FIFA World Cup championship.Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year – Cata Coll (Barcelona / Spain): Coll anchored Barcelona Femení’s defensive wall during their relentless continental trophy pursuit, keeping a record number of clean sheets.Men’s Coach of the Year – Luis de la Fuente (Spain): De la Fuente secured the honour seamlessly after leading La Roja to a flawless, undefeated World Cup campaign.Women’s Coach of the Year – Pere Romeu (Barcelona): Romeu was recognized for flawlessly maintaining Barcelona's untouchable standard of modern tactical supremacy in his debut seasons.Men’s Club of the Year – Paris Saint-Germain: PSG made history as the first team to win back-to-back Men’s Club of the Year awards, driven by an incredible five-trophy haul, deep squad depth, and domestic dominance.Women’s Club of the Year – Barcelona Femení: The Catalan giants earned undisputed status after capturing a ruthless continental and domestic clean sweep.Socrates Award – Bukayo Saka (Arsenal / England): Saka was honoured for his global humanitarian work, specifically his partnership with the charity BigShoe to fund vital medical aid and 120 life-changing children's surgeries in Nigeria.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Britain Covey ruled out of Eagles-Cowboys MNF game
articles.summary: The Eagles will be without their top returner for the rest of Monday night’s rivalry game.
articles.body:
The Cowboys were forced to settle for a field goal on the first drive against the Eagles on Monday Night Football , and unfortunately, on the kick-off that followed the first points of the game, Britain Covey was injured on the return. He was listed as questionable to return with a knee injury shortly afterward, with return duties going to Dameon Pierce and Elijah Mitchell.

It only took 13 minutes for the Eagles to rule Covey out of the rest of the game — that doesn't seem ideal.

Covey has dealt with several injuries since returning to Philadelphia this offseason, but has consistently been the team's best option on kick returns. He also provided some much-needed depth at wide receiver — even though he's at the bottom of the depth chart, with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks sidelined, there's always a chance Covey is needed on offense.

Hopefully, Covey doesn't have to deal with this injury long term, and is able to get back sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Paul Finebaum Unloads After Clemson’s Latest ACC Meltdown
articles.summary: A loss by Dabo Swinney once sent shockwaves through the college football landscape. Today, according to ESPN commentator Paul Finebaum, it barely draws a rea...
articles.body:
A loss by Dabo Swinney once sent shockwaves through the college football landscape. Today, according to ESPN commentator Paul Finebaum, it barely draws a reaction.

Clemson's 20-16 defeat at home to Virginia Tech on Saturday marked its third loss of the year, dropping the Tigers to 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play. The defeat effectively crushed Clemson's ACC championship hopes and playoff aspirations for the 2026 season—and signaled to national observers that the program's aura of invincibility is gone.

Appearing on The Matt Barrie Show, Finebaum noted that the national dialogue around Swinney's program has shifted from astonishment to complete indifference, a stark contrast to how fans and pundits once reacted to high-profile upsets.

"I'll just mention Dabo one more time," Finebaum said. "But there was a time when a Dabo Swinney loss was treated the same way as a Nick Saban loss. I mean, it sent shivers. And now it's like, OK, was that three? Was that four? And who cares?"

The indifference reflects a stark statistical drop-off. During Clemson's dynastic run from 2015 to 2020, Swinney led the Tigers to an astonishing 79-7 record, capturing six consecutive ACC championships, securing six straight College Football Playoff bids, and winning two national titles.

Since 2021, however, that dominance has unraveled. Counting a 7-6 finish in 2025 and their current 4-3 mark, the Tigers have dropped 23 games over the last five-plus seasons. During that span, Clemson has reached the playoff just once and has managed a 10-win season only once over the last three years.

Finebaum's assessment was echoed by host Matt Barrie, who voiced bewilderment over how a perennial powerhouse quietly transformed into a mid-tier competitor, especially in contrast to the momentum built by opponents like James Franklin and Virginia Tech.

"The level with which that program has kind of altered itself into being average is — I didn't think I'd see the day," Barrie said. "I thought Clemson was set up perfectly for — I mean, maybe they'll come back in the 24-team playoff era. But the fall of Clemson, and then James Franklin doing what he's doing at Virginia Tech."

With their championship goals wiped off the board, Swinney and the Tigers must regroup on the road. Clemson travels to Tallahassee, Fla., this Saturday to face Florida State at Doak Campbell Stadium (7 p.m., ACC Network).

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez arrives in Saudi Arabia for fight despite travel warning
articles.summary: The deadly conflict between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen's Houthi rebels is not deterring Canelo Alvarez from fighting on Saturday.
articles.body:
Boxing star Canelo Alvarez arrived in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia Monday, Oct. 26 for his upcoming fight without mention of a far more serious conflict.

Alvarez is moving forward with his boxing match against WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli despite deadly missile and drone strikes between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen's Houthi rebels backed by Iran.

On Oct. 10, at least 12 people were killed and more than 300 injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, according to BBC. Other airports have been attacked, and it's unclear which airport Alvarez arrived at.

"I feel great,'' Alvarez, the 36-year-old from Mexico, told Reuters. "I can't wait to step in the ring."

The U.S. Department of State has issued a travel advisory that reads, "Reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to ongoing risks of drone and missile targeting by Iran and Iran-backed Houthi rebels, armed conflict, terrorism, and strict local laws.''

But reports about Alvarez's arrival indicated he is focused on his fight set for Oct. 31, not the violence leading to the U.S. State Department travel advisory.

But a title bout on the undercard was canceled because of apparent safety concerns, according to multiple reports.

Lindolfo Delgado, who was scheduled to fight Arthur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF super lightweight bout, has remained in the United States, according to Lance Pugmire of Boxing Scene.

Sports events in Saudi Arabia that have been postponed or rescheduled include The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition, the PIF Saudi International Asian Tour golf tournament and Al Nassr's AFC Champions League Elite soccer match against ​UAE team Al Wasl.

Alvarez, a former two-time undisputed super middleweight champion, will fight for the first time since losing to Terence Crawford in September 2025.

"I think my body needed that kind of rest,'' Alvarez told Reuters, "and now I feel like it has been 10 years without fighting, so I just can't wait to step ​in the ring."

Referring to his loss to Crawford by unanimous decision, Alvarez also said, "Little mistakes are the difference between winning and losing ... I know what I did in the last fight," ​he said. "The week of the fight my mind wasn't there ​but ... ⁠things happen, I learn and that's it, we need to move forward."

Mbilli, at 31, is five years younger than Alvarez and is 29-0-1 with 24 knockouts.
